title: Summing per-layer failure bounds
statement: Let $\alpha \ge 0$, let $s \in \bbn$, and consider $m$ stages with layer sizes $\ell_0, \ldots, \ell_{m-1} \in \bbn$ whose total does not exceed $s$, i.e. $\sum_{i} \ell_i \le s$. Suppose real numbers $b_0, \ldots, b_{m-1}$ satisfy $b_i \le \ell_i\,\alpha$ for every $i$. Then $\sum_{i} b_i \le s\,\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: m stages with natural-number layer sizes
sum of layer sizes is at most s
each per-stage bound b_i is at most (layer size i)·α
replaced:
If over $m$ stages each failure bound satisfies
$\mathrm{failure\_bound}(i)\le (\mathrm{layer\_size}(i))\cdot\alpha$ with
$\alpha\ge 0$, and $\sum_i \mathrm{layer\_size}(i)\le s$, then
$\sum_i \mathrm{failure\_bound}(i)\le s\cdot\alpha$.
